issues.legal_issue: Ejectment may be granted on a permissive-occupation basis even when that basis was not expressly pleaded, if it was substantively tried and both parties had a fair opportunity to address it.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought ejectment on the basis of a tenancy, while the defendant admitted the plaintiff's ownership and claimed that his own possession rested on an agreement allowing him to remain until construction costs were repaid.
Both parties presented evidence about the basis on which the defendant occupied the premises.
The tenancy was not proved, and the defendant's asserted repayment condition was rejected, leaving the permissive character of his possession established.
The defendant did not identify any defence he could have raised had the plaintiff expressly pleaded permissive occupation in the alternative.
issues.conclusion: The decree for ejectment was properly confirmed on the basis that the defendant occupied the premises with the plaintiff's permission.
issues.legal_principle: Relief generally must rest on the parties' pleadings and the issues framed for trial. However, a court may relax the formal requirement of an express pleading where the ground was in substance in issue, both parties knew it was being tried and had an opportunity to lead evidence, and reliance on it causes no prejudice. The Court distinguished Trojan & Co. Ltd. v. Rm. N. N. Nagappa Chettiar, which rejected a new and inconsistent claim, and referred to the same principle in Sheodhar Rai & Others v. Suraj Prasad Singh & Others. It also noted the Allahabad High Court decisions in Abdul Ghani v. Musammat Babni and Balmakund v. Dalu, which permitted ejectment where tenancy was unproved but permissive occupation was established.

rule.if: ejectment_suit and alternative_ground_was_substantively_tried and both_parties_knew_ground_was_in_issue and both_parties_had_opportunity_to_lead_evidence and defendant_admitted_permissive_possession and asserted_possession_condition_was_rejected

predicates.ejectment_suit: The proceeding sought to recover possession from an occupant.
predicates.alternative_ground_was_substantively_tri: The basis for relief not expressly pleaded was nevertheless addressed in substance at trial.
predicates.both_parties_knew_ground_was_in_issue: Both parties understood that the alternative basis for relief was involved in the trial.
predicates.both_parties_had_opportunity_to_lead_evi: Each party had an opportunity to present evidence about that basis for relief.
predicates.defendant_admitted_permissive_possession: The occupant acknowledged that possession originated with the owner's permission.
predicates.asserted_possession_condition_was_reject: The occupant's claimed condition limiting the permission to remain was not established.

issues.definition: When an ejectment proceeding substantively tries an alternative ground that both parties understood and could address, and permissive possession is admitted while its asserted condition is rejected, ejectment may be granted on that ground.

issues.legal_issue: A claim for past rent cannot succeed when the alleged tenancy and its terms have not been established.
material_facts: The plaintiff claimed past rent on the basis that the defendant was a tenant.
The High Court was not satisfied that the tenancy or its terms had been established and rejected the claim for past rent.
The Supreme Court found no reason to interfere with that rejection.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the claim for past rent was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to interfere with the High Court's rejection of past rent because the alleged tenancy and its terms had not been established. The High Court had also observed that, under the relevant U.P. control-of-rent legislation and the preceding Ordinance, letting premises required permission from the competent authority and a tenancy without that permission would be invalid; the Supreme Court did not separately elaborate on that statutory point.

predicates.past_rent_claim_in_ejectment_suit: A claimant sought past rent in a proceeding also seeking ejectment.
predicates.alleged_tenancy_and_its_terms_not_establ: The claimant failed to establish the alleged tenancy and the terms on which rent was said to be due.

issues.definition: When past rent is claimed in an ejectment proceeding but the alleged tenancy and its terms are not established, the past-rent claim is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: A decree granting ejectment must provide compensation for the occupant's continued use of the property after the decree until possession is delivered.
material_facts: The plaintiff became entitled to eject the defendant.
The defendant remained in possession after the decree for ejectment.
The trial court had assessed a reasonable monthly amount for use and occupation, and the Supreme Court saw no reason to differ from that assessment.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was awarded future mesne profits at the trial court's assessed rate from the date of its ejectment decree until delivery of possession.
issues.legal_principle: Once ejectment is granted, an occupant who remains in possession despite the decree must pay mesne profits or damages for use and occupation from the date of the decree until delivery of possession. A decree for ejectment in such a case must include a direction for that payment.

predicates.ejectment_proceeding: The proceeding seeks recovery of possession from an occupant.
predicates.ejectment_decree_granted: The court has granted an order requiring the occupant to give up possession.
predicates.occupant_remains_in_possession_after_dec: The occupant continues to hold the property after the ejectment order.

issues.definition: If an ejectment proceeding results in an ejectment decree and the occupant remains in possession afterward, compensation for that continued occupation must be awarded.
